title: NovaPay POC scoping - workload & benchmarks
next_steps: Send Dedicated sizing and pricing sheet
Schedule benchmark run (synthetic + prod trace) for 2025-12-09
Draft POC success criteria and timeline (2-4 weeks)
action_items: Jordan Lee: prepare benchmark script and container image (due 2025-12-09)
Lydia Park: send pricing + dedicated sizing doc (due 2025-12-06)
Priya Raman: share anonymized production trace and QPS targets (due 2025-12-08)
Akash Patel: provide network egress limits and VPC peering window (due 2025-12-07)
summary: POC scoping focused on traffic modeling (QPS, concurrency), token distributions, and benchmark plan. Discussed success criteria: p95 latency SLOs, cost targets, and timeline for a 2-4 week pilot. Agreed next steps: share sizing/pricing, run synthetic + prod-trace benchmarks, and finalize success criteria.
transcript:
[00:00] Lydia (Redwood AE): Alright everyone, thanks for joining, we can kick off. Quick intro, I'm Lydia, AE on the account. Jordan's our SE.
[00:12] Priya (NovaPay): Hi, Priya here, Head of ML. Thanks y'all. We got Tom and Akash and Sara on as well.
[00:20] Jordan (Redwood SE): Hey team. Today our goal is to scope the POC workload modeling — get clear QPS, concurrency, token distributions, success criteria and a realistic benchmark plan.
[00:33] Tom (Customer): Quick note, we're mainly focused on payment auth flows and invoice summarization. Auth is hot path, sub 200ms preferred, summaries can be a few hundred ms.
[00:45] Lydia: Good. Can you share current numbers — QPS, typical request size, concurrency?
[00:52] Priya: Sure. For auth flows we peak at ~120 QPS presently during batch windows, sustained 20-30 QPS outside. Concurrency roughly 60 concurrent requests at peak because we fanout to downstream checks. Token wise auth prompts are small — 80 to 150 input tokens, output around 20-40. For summarization, input is 800-2,000 tokens, output 150-300.
[01:17] Jordan: Okay that's helpful. When you say 120 QPS peak is that per region or global?
[01:22] Priya: That's global, ~70% in US east, 20% eu-west, 10% ap-something.
[01:28] Akash: Our SRE constraint is outbound bandwidth and also we have strict VPC peering windows for the on-prem flows.
[01:35] Lydia: Noted. For POC, do you want Redwood Hosted API or Dedicated reserved capacity?
[01:40] Sara (Product): We're open to either, but for the pilot we'd probably prefer Hosted to move faster; if performance/costs don't meet targets we may move to Dedicated.
[01:49] Jordan: Great. For Hosted we can run a realistic synthetic load, and we can also replay an anonymized trace if you provide one — that helps measure prefix/kv cache hit rates and average token per request distribution.
[02:00] Priya: We'll provide an anonymized trace. Question: how do you model concurrency vs QPS? We want to understand if 120 QPS with 60 concurrency is realistic for inference servers.
[02:10] Jordan: We'll model both. Key variables: model latency per token, batching window and concurrency per connection. With continuous batching, higher QPS increases effective throughput but might bump p95 if batch windows increase; dedicated GPUs lower jitter. For auth flows with small outputs, batching gains are less, but GPU context switching and warm KV cache matter.
[02:30] Tom: We're concerned about p95 latency spikes — our SLA to customers is 250ms for auth.
[02:36] Lydia: For success criteria let's capture that explicitly: auth p95 <= 250ms end-to-end, summarization p95 <= 1s, correctness fuzz with Rouge-like metric not dropping more than 5% vs baseline, and cost per 1M tokens below your threshold — what is that threshold?
[02:51] Priya: We'd like cost to be no more than $X per 1M tokens — ok to discuss offline, we'll give a number. For MVP we'd tolerate higher cost if latency is met.
[02:59] Jordan: Understood. For workload characterization we'll ask for: production trace, distribution of input/output token lengths, per-route QPS, and fraction of requests that hit cache.
[03:09] Priya: Fraction of cache hits is hard to give but we estimate ~30% prefix repetition for auth due to templated prompts, summaries lower.
[03:17] Jordan: Good, that helps. For the POC benchmark plan we propose three phases: 1) synthetic QPS sweep (step-load to 2x peak), 2) prod-trace replay to measure realistic batching/KV behavior, 3) end-to-end integration test from your API gateway to measure latency SLO.
[03:34] Lydia: Timeline? We can turn around synthetic tests in 2-3 days once we have scripts; trace run and analysis another week, and end-to-end integration in parallel if you can open network peering. So 2-4 weeks total.
[03:47] Akash: Network peering windows are next Tuesday and Thursday, we can aim for the Tuesday window.
[03:53] Jordan: Perfect. A few technical clarifications on modeling: what's your average prompt tokenization pattern — are system prompts included, or do you do client-side prompt templating?
[04:03] Priya: We include a 40-token system context for auth; user prompt ~60 tokens dynamic. Summaries include the full doc content.
[04:12] Jordan: Ok so auth total input ~140 including system. That matches earlier numbers. We'll also measure prefix cache hit rate effect by replaying repeated auth prompts. Note: our KV cache for LLMs reduces repeated prefix computation, so effective latency may be much better on repeated traffic. We'll try both cold and warm cache scenarios.
[04:30] Tom: Can you also simulate concurrency bursts? We see bursts from 50 to 200 concurrent connections during settlement windows.
[04:36] Jordan: Yes, we'll include burst profiles. For instance: steady-state 30 QPS with occasional 2-minute bursts to 200 QPS. We'll measure p50/p90/p95/p99 and token throughput.
[04:47] Priya: What's your suggestion for model family? We want good safety and hallucination characteristics for summaries but auth is tolerant.
[04:53] Jordan: For Pilot we recommend a two-track approach: a smaller, faster quantized variant for auth (e.g., a quantized 7B family) and a higher-quality 13B or open-llm variant for summaries. We can fallback from Hosted to a cheaper variant when cost spikes.
[05:06] Lydia: Also mention Dedicated — if you choose Dedicated we can allocate reserved GPUs to guarantee tail latency and throughput. That reduces variability but requires commit. For pilots we usually start Hosted then evaluate Dedicated sizing.
[05:19] Akash: Security question: do you support VPC peering and customer-managed KMS?
[05:24] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Private and Dedicated support VPC and customer KMS/HSM. For Hosted we have encryption at rest and SOC2 — we can share SOC2 and network diagrams.
[05:34] Priya: Please share SOC2 and the audit logs format. We need to show this to InfoSec.
[05:39] Lydia: We'll attach SOC2, ISO summary and a sample audit log schema.
[05:44] Tom: For the benchmark, what metrics should we capture besides latency and throughput?
[05:49] Jordan: We capture token cost per request, GPU utilization, batch size distribution, KV cache hit rate, and failure/error rates. We'll correlate cost with latency.
[05:58] Priya: On token distributions, summarization has a long tail — about 5-10% of docs are >1,500 tokens. Need to ensure you can handle the tail without causing downstream backpressure.
[06:10] Jordan: We'll run tests with a long-tail distribution: 85% under 800 tokens, 10% 800-1,500, 5% >1,500. We'll also test sequence-length-limited variants (chunking) and measure accuracy drop.
[06:23] Lydia: Regarding success criteria, let's write them out so we can align:
- Auth p95 end-to-end <= 250ms
- Summarization p95 <= 1s
- Quality delta vs baseline < 5% (your internal metric)
- Error rate < 0.1% in POC runs
- Cost target TBD by Priya
[06:40] Priya: That looks good. We'll send the baseline metrics.
[06:44] Sara: For artifacts, Jordan, will you send the benchmark harness or do you want us to run it?
[06:50] Jordan: We'll provide the benchmark harness as a container and a script. Ideally you run it against a staging endpoint and we run the hosted replay; we can also run an automated replay in Redwood infra if you prefer.
[07:01] Akash: We need the exact network ports and peering steps for the SRE team.
[07:06] Lydia: We'll include a network checklist and required CIDR blocks in the doc.
[07:11] Tom: Cost modeling question — how do you estimate token costs for the Dedicated case? We prefer a per-GPU/hour and amortized token cost.
[07:19] Jordan: For Dedicated we provide sizing recommendations: expected QPS per GPU for the model family, expected effective tokens/sec, and then you can compute GPU hours. We'll provide a sample spreadsheet that maps QPS/concurrency to GPU count and estimated hours and cost.
[07:33] Priya: For the POC we just need a rough estimate so procurement can sign off.
[07:38] Lydia: We'll include a sample TCO spreadsheet.
[07:42] Jordan: A couple more modeling details: 1) batching window: we'll test both low-latency windows (<5ms) and relaxed batching to maximize throughput; 2) KV cache warm vs cold; 3) multi-region routing for latencies. We'll provide per-region latency estimates.
[07:59] Priya: Regarding multiregion, can you route to nearest region and failover if capacity spikes?
[08:05] Jordan: Yes, smart routing can route by policy (latency/cost/region). For failover we can configure fallback to a cheaper variant or different region. We'll include an example policy for NovaPay.
[08:16] Tom: Any caveats around tokenization differences between models? We saw slight token count variations between model families which affected cost.
[08:24] Jordan: Good call. We'll normalize to a consistent tokenization baseline or measure actual token counts per family and show adjustments in the spreadsheet.
[08:33] Akash: For data privacy, we need to confirm whether requests/responses are logged and retention period.
[08:39] Lydia: Hosted logs are retained per account policy; we offer configurable retention and can disable request/response logging for sensitive routes. We'll share the retention options and the audit log format.
[08:50] Priya: For the replay, we'll scrub PII and share an anonymized trace.
[08:55] Jordan: Perfect. For the synthetic load we'll seed a mix of auth and summary traffic with your provided distributions: auth: 70% of requests small tokens, summary: 30% large tokens. We'll run a QPS sweep: 0.5x, 1x, 1.5x, 2x and bursts up to 3x for 60s.
[09:14] Lydia: Who will be responsible for scheduling the SRE peering window? Akash?
[09:17] Akash: Yes, I'll coordinate. We can target Tuesday next week.
[09:21] Lydia: Great. On the security docs — I'll drop SOC2 and the sample audit logs to the thread after the call.
[09:28] Priya: Another question: can you measure p99 tail latencies and provide breakdown of where time is spent (token generation vs network vs batching)?
[09:36] Jordan: Yes, we'll instrument and provide breakdowns. For p99, Dedicated usually helps most but we also look at batching variance and model step time.
[09:45] Tom: For the pilot, what does success look like to Redwood?
[09:49] Lydia: Success for us is demonstrating predictable latency and unit economics that are at least close to your targets, and producing a recommended path (Hosted -> Dedicated) with clear sizing. Then we hope to progress to a committed Dedicated engagement.
[10:00] Priya: Sounds fair. Can we also include a short user acceptance test where product runs typical flows with real user-like inputs?
[10:07] Jordan: Absolutely, we'll include UAT scenarios in the benchmark plan. We can provide test cases and acceptance thresholds.
[10:14] Sara: Timeline recap?
[10:16] Lydia: We'll ship pricing and sizing by 2025-12-06. You (Priya) will share anonymized trace and QPS distribution by 2025-12-08. Jordan will prepare benchmark harness by 2025-12-09 and target the first synthetic run on 2025-12-09. Full trace run and analysis by 2025-12-16, with recommendations the following week. That aligns with a 2-4 week POC.
[10:36] Akash: That timeline works.
[10:38] Priya: One more thing — can you show examples of fallback policies and how they affect user-visible latency?
[10:45] Jordan: Yes we'll model a policy where requests first try high-quality model in US-east, if capacity>threshold or latency>target then failover to quantized 7B or to another region; we'll show cost and latency differences.
[10:58] Lydia: We'll include a sample policy and expected outcomes table.
[11:02] Tom: Anything else?
[11:04] Priya: No, thanks. This was useful.
[11:07] Lydia: Recap next steps: Lydia send pricing/SOC2/docs, Jordan prepare harness + run synthetic and trace replays, Priya share trace and cost thresholds, Akash schedule peering. We'll capture action items in the thread.
[11:19] Lydia: Alright, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the deck and links.
[11:24] Sara: Thanks all.
[11:26] (call ends)

Notes and artifacts referenced: "Redwood POC benchmark harness" (link: https://redwood.example/benchmarks/novapay - placeholder), "Dedicated sizing spreadsheet" (attached), SOC2 audit summary (attached).

Transcription notes: occasional mis-attributions (Speaker 2 labeled as Jordan in a few segments), small ASR errors: "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "KV cash", some punctuation missing."
